arxiv-1701-05771.title: Strongly screening on electron capture for Nuclides 52,53,59,60 Fe by the Shell-Model Monte Carlo method in pre-supernova
arxiv-1701-05771.creator: Jing-Jing, Liu e1,addr1, Qiu-He, Peng 2, Dong-Mei, Liu addr1
arxiv-1701-05771.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Jing-Jing, Liu e1,addr1, Qiu-He, Peng 2, Dong-Mei, Liu addr1. The death of the massive stars due to supernova explosion is a key ingredient in stellar evolution, stellar population synthesis. The electron capture (EC) plays a vital role in supernovae explosions. According to the Shell-Model Monte Carlo (SMMC) method , basing on the Random Phase Approximation (RPA) and Linear Response Theory Model (LRTM), we study the strongly screening EC rates of nuclides 52,53,59,60 Fe in presupernova.

arxiv-2103-08265.title: Constant Random Perturbations Provide Adversarial Robustness with Minimal Effect on Accuracy
arxiv-2103-08265.creator: Bronya Roni Chernyak, Bhiksha Raj, Tamir Hazan, Joseph Keshet
arxiv-2103-08265.description: Abstract This paper proposes an attack-independent (non-adversarial training) technique for improving adversarial robustness of neural network models, with minimal loss of standard accuracy. We suggest creating a neighborhood around each training example, such that the label is kept constant for all inputs within that neighborhood.

arxiv-2207-13222.title: Information We Can Extract About a User From ‘One Minute Mobile Application Usage’
arxiv-2207-13222.creator: Sarwan Ali
arxiv-2207-13222.description: Abstract Understanding human behavior is an important task and has applications in many domains such as targeted advertisement, health analytics, security, and entertainment, etc. For this purpose, designing a system for activity recognition (AR) is important. However, since every human can have different behaviors, understanding and analyzing common patterns become a challenging task.

arxiv-2302-03371.creator: Zs. M. Szabó, Y. Gong, K. M. Menten, W. Yang, C. J. Cyganowski, Á. Kóspál, P. Ábrahám, A. Belloche, F. Wyrowski

In both cases, outbursts of several magnitudes are observed, which are attributed to enhanced mass accretion from the circumstellar disk onto the central protostar.

arxiv-2308-07517.description: Abstract . Efficiently reviewing scholarly literature and synthesizing prior art are crucial for scientific progress. arxiv-2404-16273.title: Structured Nonsmooth Optimization Using Functional Encoding and Branching Information
arxiv-2404-16273.creator: Fengqiao Luo
arxiv-2404-16273.description: Abstract We develop a novel gradient-based algorithm for optimizing nonsmooth nonconvex functions where nonsmoothness arises from explicit nonsmooth operators in the objective’s analytical form. Our key innovation involves encoding active smooth branches of these operators, enabling both branch function extraction at arbitrary points and transition detection through branch tracking.

arxiv-2501-03796.title: Mixing by Internal Gravity Waves in Stars: Assessing Numerical Simulations Against Theory
arxiv-2501-03796.creator: J. Morton, T. Guillet, I. Baraffe, A. Morison, A. Le Saux, D.G. Vlaykov, T. Goffrey, J. Pratt
arxiv-2501-03796.description: Abstract Here we present a study of radial chemical mixing in non-rotating massive main-sequence stars driven by internal gravity waves (IGWs) , based on multi-dimensional hydrodynamical simulations with the fully compressible code MUSIC. We examine two proposed mechanisms of material mixing in stars by IGWs that are commonly quoted, relating to thermal diffusion and sub-wavelength shearing.

arxiv-2501-12048.title: Adaptive Class Learning to Screen Diabetic Disorders in Fundus Images of Eye Thanks: This research was supported by the J. C. Bose National Fellowship, grant no. JCB/2020/000033 of S. Mitra.
arxiv-2501-12048.creator: Shramana Dey, Pallabi Dutta, Riddhasree Bhattacharyya, Surochita Pal, Sushmita Mitra, Rajiv Raman
arxiv-2501-12048.description: Abstract The prevalence of ocular illnesses is growing globally, presenting a substantial public health challenge. Early detection and timely intervention are crucial for averting visual impairment and enhancing patient prognosis. This research introduces a new framework called Class Extension with Limited Data (CELD) to train a classifier to categorize retinal fundus images.

arxiv-2512-15207.title: Remote Magnetic Levitation Using Reduced Attitude Control and Parametric Field Models
arxiv-2512-15207.creator: Neelaksh Singh, Jasan Zughaibi, Denis von Arx, Bradley J. Nelson, Michael Muehlebach
arxiv-2512-15207.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Neelaksh Singh, Jasan Zughaibi, Denis von Arx, Bradley J. Nelson, Michael Muehlebach. Electromagnetic navigation systems (eMNS) are increasingly used in minimally invasive procedures such as endovascular interventions and targeted drug delivery due to their ability to generate fast and precise magnetic fields. In this paper, we utilize the OctoMag eMNS to achieve remote levitation and control of a rigid body across large air gaps which showcases the dynamic capabilities of clinical eMNS.

pmc-10548264.title: Stage shift and relative survival for head and neck cancer during the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic: a population-based study of temporal trends
pmc-10548264.creator: Hanna M. Peacock, Cindy De Gendt, Geert Silversmit, Sandra Nuyts, Jan Casselman, Jean-Pascal Machiels, Francesco Giusti, Bart van Gool, Vincent Vander Poorten, Liesbet Van Eycken
pmc-10548264.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). ObjectiveDuring the first wave of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, non-essential health services were suspended in Belgium, and the public was ordered to socially isolate. Underdiagnosis of cancer during this period was reported worldwide. Certain risk factors for head and neck cancer (HNC) overlap with those for COVID-19 incidence and mortality, making underdiagnosis and subsequent stage shift of this potentially rapidly progressing cancer a major concern.

pmc-11712769.title: Characterization of pulsations in the brain and cerebrospinal fluid using ultra‐high field magnetic resonance imaging
pmc-11712769.creator: Bruno de Almeida, Tiago Amaro Martins, Minjie Wu, Kristine A Wilckens, Davneet S Minhas, James W Ibinson, Howard J Aizenstein, Tales Santini, Tamer S Ibrahim
pmc-11712769.description: BackgroundBrain fluid flow plays a crucial role in maintaining brain health by eliminating potentially harmful waste products like amyloid‐beta and tau [1‐2]. pmc-12694947.title: Transparent Reporting of AI in Systematic Literature Reviews: Development of the PRISMA-trAIce Checklist
pmc-12694947.creator: Dirk Holst, Keno Moenck, Julian Koch, Ole Schmedemann, Thorsten Schüppstuhl
pmc-12694947.description: BackgroundSystematic literature reviews (SLRs) build the foundation for evidence synthesis, but they are exceptionally demanding in terms of time and resources. While recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models, offer the potential to accelerate this process, their use introduces challenges to transparency and reproducibility.

pmc-12820182.title: Gradient chaotropic regulation of Zn2+ solvation chemistry for low-temperature zinc metal batteries
pmc-12820182.creator: Sinian Yang, Shunshun Zhao, Haojie Xu, Xinwei Wang, Xuanrui Huang, Qi Yang, Yong Chen, Guoxiu Wang, Shimou Chen
pmc-12820182.description: Aqueous zinc-ion batteries have emerged as a promising system for safe and sustainable energy storage. However, their practical application is hindered by detrimental interfacial side reactions and inadequate low-temperature performance. Herein, we report the design of a gradient chaotropic ionic liquid (IL)-based aqueous electrolyte (Emim⁺-TFA⁻/OTf⁻-Zn2+-H2O), which can simultaneously fulfil the conflicting demands of dendrite-free zinc deposition and low-temperature operation.

pmc-13124786.title: Mechanical traumatic injuries as a cause of death in free-ranging neotropical non-human primates living in anthropogenic matrices
pmc-13124786.creator: Rafaela Magalhães Barros, Isabel Luana de Macêdo, Davi Emanuel Ribeiro de Sousa, Yasmin Nunes Godoy da Fonseca, Liz de Albuquerque Cerqueira, Gabriela Rodrigues de Toledo Costa, Liria Queiroz Luz Hirano, Márcio Botelho de Castro
pmc-13124786.description: Traumatic injuries are a major cause of morbidity and mortality in free-ranging non-human primates (NHPs), often associated with anthropogenic pressures such as habitat loss, urbanization, and interactions with domestic animals. This study characterized some epidemiological, spatial, and pathological patterns of mechanical traumatic injuries in free-ranging non-human primates from anthropogenically altered areas of the Federal District.

pmc-13190781.title: Lactate metabolism and lactylation in cancer: from pathogenesis to therapeutic advances
pmc-13190781.creator: Chunyao Fang, Suiqing Zhou, Kai Yu, Liren Zhang, Wenxin Lian, Xiaofeng Tie, Shu Chen, Jingjing Dai, Qing Li, Xuehao Wang
pmc-13190781.description: Lactate and its mediated modification, lactylation, are receiving increasing attention in the field of tumor biology. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the mechanistic involvement of lactate and lactylation in key oncogenic processes, such as tumor initiation, proliferation, invasion, metastasis, recurrence, and drug resistance.

pmc-13466101.title: Plasma Proteomic Signatures in Alkaptonuria
pmc-13466101.creator: Rebecca Finetti, Anna Visibelli, Bianca Roncaglia, Alfonso Trezza, Luana Peruzzi, Barbara Marzocchi, Ottavia Spiga, Mattia Cicogni, Laura Salvini, Laura Tinti, Vittoria Cicaloni, Sara Cheleschi, Marco Rossi, Cristina Tinti, Annalisa Santucci
pmc-13466101.description: Simple SummaryAlkaptonuria (AKU) is a rare inherited metabolic disorder caused by the accumulation of homogentisic acid, which progressively damages cartilage and other connective tissues.
